claim: PH is a chronic, progressive condition characterised by elevated pulmonary arterial pressure.
source: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a chronic, progressive condition characterised by elevated pulmonary arterial pressure, primarily resulting from pulmonary vascular remodelling.
evidence: This is a general medical definition supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: PH primarily results from pulmonary vascular remodelling driven by infiltration of inflammatory cells, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and hyperplasia of the pulmonary intima.
source: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a chronic, progressive condition characterised by elevated pulmonary arterial pressure, primarily resulting from pulmonary vascular remodelling. This remodelling is driven by the infiltration of inflammatory cells, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and hyperplasia of the pulmonary intima (Rubin and Naeije, 2023; Shah et al., 2023; Simonneau et al., 2019).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by cited literature.

claim: Approximately 1% of the adult population is affected by PH.

claim: High altitude typically signifies a hypoxic environment due to the decrease in barometric pressure as altitude increases.
